The roots of this idea lie in epistemologyâthe study of knowledge. Last Thursdayism draws from philosophical skepticism, particularly the problem of induction and the limitations of empirical evidence. Itâs closely related to Descartesâ evil demon hypothesis or the brain-in-a-vat scenario. Essentially, it confronts us with a mind-bending question: can you prove the past really happened? Just because everything appears consistent with a long history doesnât guarantee that history occurred. Maybe your memories were implanted. Maybe your birth certificate, old photos, and your scars are all part of the illusion.

Though itâs a mental exercise, Last Thursdayism has deeper implications. It reveals how fragile our trust in reality is, relying on senses and memories that could theoretically be deceived. But rather than leading us to nihilism, it can encourage humilityâreminding us that certainty is rare and that questioning our beliefs is healthy.
